name: Cephalexin
summary: First-generation oral cephalosporin; first-line for uncomplicated skin and soft-tissue infections and uncomplicated UTI.
mechanism: Beta-lactam inhibition of penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) blocks peptidoglycan cross-linking during cell-wall synthesis.

dosing.adult: 250-500 mg PO every 6 hours (e.g. 500 mg q6h for cellulitis; 250 mg q6h for uncomplicated UTI)

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cephalosporins (caution with penicillin allergy)
warnings: Cross-reactivity with penicillin allergy (low but real)
Inactive against MRSA, Enterococcus, and atypicals

clinicalPearls: First-line for uncomplicated cellulitis — cheap, well tolerated
No MRSA, Enterococcus, or atypical coverage — culture and resistance data matter
good: Simple, well-tolerated oral therapy for skin and urinary infections.
bad: Not for MRSA, Enterococcus, or pyelonephritis; E. coli resistance limits empiric UTI use in many regions.
